A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, and all 12 pages of each support comparison of text, equations, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix or attached supplement. The supplementary tracker discussion referenced in v2 is unavailable and is not assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo-NOTR reconstruction and novel-view-synthesis results, component ablations, and an initial reconstruction-quality experiment in Tables 1–2 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original Waymo-NOTR results and reports additional KITTI evaluation and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The proposed GLEE/LiDAR tracking and fusion procedure, HexPlane motion representation, isotropic Gaussian marbles, losses and training stages remain unchanged. UNINEXT is tested as a tracker-substitution ablation; the expanded introduction explains the existing method.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from Waymo-NOTR dynamic32 alone to include independently collected KITTI street scenes, substantially broadening the empirical basis for cross-dataset applicability. KITTI-75% and KITTI-50% are two splits of this added coverage, not separate tasks.

E2.justification: NSG becomes an evaluated comparator in the new KITTI comparison, having previously appeared only in background citations. The dedicated initial-reconstruction comparison using VoxelNext boxes disappears. The five comparators in the retained NOTR Table 1 are unchanged.

E3.justification: KITTI introduces 75% and 50% training protocols, holding out every fourth or second frame. Removing the initial-reconstruction experiment also removes its object-selection, alignment and Chamfer-distance evaluation protocol. Retained NOTR image resolution, temporal split, training budgets and 3D-tracker pretraining remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's initial geometry evaluation against ground-truth-derived reconstructions, including Figure 4, has no counterpart in the supplied v2. v2 Table 3 adds a 3D-tracker-without-motion-loss control and a UNINEXT substitution experiment. These substantially revise the evidence testing motion supervision and robustness to tracker choice.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The removed reconstruction-error histogram describes variation across objects, rather than uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: All 60 numerical entries in NOTR Table 1 remain identical. New KITTI results show higher SSIM and lower LPIPS than Street Gaussians, but lower PSNR: 25.49 versus 25.79 at 75% training and 25.11 versus 25.52 at 50%. The retained 3D-tracker ablation changes from (27.55, 0.829, 24.85, 0.747) to (28.02, 0.835, 24.61, 0.746) for PSNR, SSIM, DPSNR and DSSIM. Two ablation rows are added, while the initial-reconstruction results disappear. The stated motion-loss DPSNR drop is corrected from 1.17 to 1.04 dB, and reported inference speed changes from approximately 80 to 100 FPS without an explained implementation change.

T1.justification: The mathematical construction, assumptions and losses are retained, with no added proofs or derivations. Equation 4 changes Q to the already defined object-cloud symbol O, aligning the notation with the unchanged surrounding explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion extend the performance claim from Waymo-NOTR to Waymo-NOTR and KITTI. The central contributions of eliminating reliance on 3D trackers and learning motion implicitly retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 expands the rationale for evaluating nuScenes-pretrained 3D tracking on Waymo-NOTR. It attributes the KITTI PSNR deficit to Street Gaussians' ground-truth tracking annotations and interprets the UNINEXT results as robustness to tracker choice. The initial-reconstruction interpretation disappears with that analysis; most existing mechanism explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that its pretrained 2D tracker was not trained on Waymo or KITTI and identifies the source of borrowed KITTI baseline results and their tracking annotations. Reported inference speed changes from 80 to 100 FPS. Hardware, approximately two-hour training time, hyperparameters and the promise of future code release are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the KITTI dataset article by Geiger et al. and the UNINEXT paper by Yan et al., plus supporting generalization citations in Figure 1. The related-work sections and overall positioning remain substantially unchanged; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify HexPlane motivation, expand baseline explanations and reorganize experimental settings. The initial-reconstruction section is removed, ablations become Section 4.3, and their narrative is revised. Most method and related-work prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes Figure 4, adds a full-width KITTI table, and expands and reformats the ablation table from six to eight rows, renumbering it from Table 2 to Table 3. These changes reflow the experimental pages; Figures 1–3 and the main NOTR table retain their displays.

improvement.justification: KITTI and UNINEXT evaluations strengthen support for generalization, while the added within-method motion-loss control provides more direct evidence than v1's cross-method comparison. Clearer checkpoint and baseline provenance improves transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of the direct reconstruction-error diagnostic and unexplained revisions to an existing ablation row and reported speed. The net improvement is limited, and KITTI supports metric-dependent advantages.
